By test step

✓pass✕new failure●known failure⚠job failed in setup⊘skipped: an earlier step failed–not run

A step that shows ⊘ or – for several pushes is a blind spot: the GPU's verdict cannot see it.

New failures: tests that passed on the previous push and fail now

A test is new when it failed on this push and passed on the previous push that ran its step on the same GPU. Pushes where the step was skipped or hit a setup failure do not count. On the step's next result it moves to Known, keeping the push it first failed at. The last column checks the scheduled run of the same commit: a failure it reproduces is real, one it does not is a flake candidate.

TLX ops bench (nightly-tlx-ops-bench.yml)

Times every tlx.ops op against its reference on each GPU after each nightly release. Each row is the latest run on that GPU, with the ops whose bench failed; per-case numbers are on the TLX ops bench dashboard.

Perf events from the TLX ops bench, last two nights

An event is a case whose TLX TFLOP/s moved 10% or more from one night to the next and still holds the night after. The latest night cannot be confirmed yet. Full per-kernel history is on the TLX ops bench dashboard.

Smart trigger: which GPU types each run tested

all 32 of 31 of 3none (build skipped too)

The select job picks the GPU types (H100, B200, MI350) whose code a change touches. PR and push runs should skip the rest; a "GPU suite" is one GPU type's tests in one run. Scheduled and manual runs must test all three. A fallback means the changed paths were unavailable, so every suite ran.

GPU hours and runs per day, by run outcome

passedtest failurebuild failuresetup failurecancelled

GPU hours

Runs

GPU hours are job start-to-finish time on GPU runners, all triggers. Setup failures and cancelled runs are spent GPU time that produced no test result. A build failure stops the run before its GPU jobs, so it shows in runs, not hours. Runs count only runs that used GPU time or failed the build.

GPU minutes per run

pushPRmedian per day

Push and PR runs that passed or failed tests. Cancelled runs and setup or build failures stopped early and are left out. Hover a day for the 25th and 75th percentiles. A PR run tests only the GPUs its paths touch, so the spread mixes one-GPU and all-GPU runs.

Queue time: waiting for a GPU runner (minutes)

B200H100MI350median per day

Time from a GPU job being queued to a runner picking it up, all triggers, jobs that ran. Each line is the day's median; hover a day for the 25th and 75th percentiles. "Last to finish" is how often that GPU's job was the last one on a PR run: that job decides when the PR gets its result, so its queue is the wait the queue tile reports.

Job duration, last 7 days vs the 7 before (minutes)

The slowest 10% shows stalls the median hides, such as a wheel download that stalls.
